evidence: src/domain/OrderStatus.ts defines FULFILMENT_SEQUENCE, CANCELLABLE, nextStatus() and isCancellable(). src/domain/Order.ts advanceTo() and cancel() call these functions rather than repeating the rules.
src/domain/Quantity.ts Quantity.of() is the only place that checks for a positive integer. Order.restore and Order.place build quantities through Quantity.of and Quantity.add.
src/domain/StockReservationService.ts reserve() calls product.canReserve() and product.reserve(), the abstractions src/domain/Product.ts provides, and never edits onHand or reserved directly.
src/domain/Product.ts and src/domain/Order.ts follow the same snapshot pattern: ProductSnapshot/OrderSnapshot, restore() and toSnapshot().
src/domain/errors.ts: ValidationError, NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidStateTransitionError all extend DomainError and are used throughout the module.
src/domain/Clock.ts, src/domain/IdGenerator.ts, src/domain/OrderRepository.ts and src/domain/ProductRepository.ts are small port interfaces for the same order and stock concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Every file in src/domain belongs to one concern: placing orders, moving them through fulfilment, and reserving stock for them. The ports (Clock, IdGenerator, OrderRepository, ProductRepository) are small interfaces that state what the domain needs from outside. Each invariant is defined once. The status transition rules live in OrderStatus.ts (nextStatus, isCancellable), and Order.ts calls them instead of copying them. Quantity validation happens only in Quantity.of. Stock availability is defined by Product.available and Product.canReserve. StockReservationService works through Product's own methods (canReserve, reserve, release, dispatch) rather than changing stock fields directly, so it respects the module's abstractions. The only overlap is small: the service checks every line first and throws InsufficientStockError itself so a reservation is all-or-nothing, and Product.reserve throws the same error. The rule itself still lives only in Product.canReserve, so this does not duplicate an invariant. Order and Product both use the same snapshot/restore pattern, and every error extends DomainError, so the module is consistent.
